trust_principles: Source-native bytes, text, language, layout and document versions are immutable references.
OCR, parsing, translation and semantic alignment produce candidates or proposals only.
A translated text never replaces the source text or becomes legal equivalence by automation.
Every extracted assertion must resolve to a version-pinned document anchor.
Unknown language, reading order, date, amount, negation or modality is preserved as unknown.
OCR confidence is local to tokens, blocks and pages and never establishes document authority.
Rights, privacy classification, revocation and document withdrawal override convenience and caches.
Mixed-language and mixed-script documents are segmented rather than forced into one language.
No model, parser, OCR engine, browser, connector or worker can admit canonical document facts.
Semantic parity is evaluated per dimension and per language; aggregate similarity cannot hide a critical mismatch.
Anchors fail closed on document-version, content-digest, geometry or quote-digest mismatch.
Canonical admission requires independent runtime checks and explicit human document authority.

rules: BCP 47 language tags and script are explicit.
Locale is not inferred from country alone.
Negation, modality, amounts, dates, named entities and taxonomy codes are critical dimensions.
A missing critical dimension produces REVIEW_REQUIRED or DENY, never PASS.
Machine translation preserves source text, model version, prompt profile and confidence.
Native extraction is attempted before OCR unless the format profile requires OCR.
Raw and extracted payload persistence follows the source-rights snapshot.
Hidden text layers and rendered pages are compared when both exist.
Reading order is explicit and reversible.
Tables preserve row, column, span, header and page geometry.
Parser output without raw-reference lineage is quarantined.
Confidence is never averaged across a critical low-confidence span.
OCR fallback does not overwrite a valid native text layer.
Image preprocessing is versioned and reversible.
Handwriting and unsupported scripts are marked unsupported or review-required.
Invisible-text disagreement, prompt injection and executable content are quarantined.
OCR engine upgrades require fixture replay before use.
Document version and content digest must match exactly.
Page indices and geometry are validated against the rendered version.
Quote digests bind normalized text without replacing source text.
Table-cell anchors include row, column and span coordinates.
A stale or ambiguous anchor contributes zero canonical evidence.
Document amendment or withdrawal invalidates dependent currentness claims.
Parity is directional and version-pinned.
Each dimension is MATCH, MISMATCH, UNKNOWN or NOT_APPLICABLE.
Critical MISMATCH produces DENY.
Critical UNKNOWN produces REVIEW_REQUIRED.
Non-critical mismatches remain explicit and cannot be hidden by an aggregate score.
Round-trip translation is diagnostic only and cannot approve parity.
Canonical writes require active human approval and deterministic runtime validation.
The least-authoritative input bounds every derived object.
Revoked, withdrawn, superseded or rights-denied material contributes zero to new decisions.
Human review does not waive rights, privacy, anchor or version requirements.
Tenant-private proposals cannot mutate the global admitted ledger.
Unknown classification defaults to RESTRICTED.
Secrets are not persisted in extracted text, logs, fixtures or exports.
Personal data detection proposes classification and cannot lower it.
OCR and parser processes are non-root, isolated and network-denied by default.
Document content cannot alter tools, prompts, network policy or admission decisions.
Thresholds are language, document-class and extractor-version specific.
Unknown quality metrics do not pass.
A critical span below threshold is not masked by document-level averages.
Regression of any admitted profile suspends new materialisation.
Fixtures include born-digital, scanned, mixed-language, tables and amended documents.

required_before_canonical_activation: P05 dependency accepted or explicitly superseded by a normative ADR
P04, P03, P02 and P01 transitive dependencies satisfied or explicitly superseded
six-language profile and parity dimensions validated
native extraction, OCR fallback and layout lineage tests PASS
anchor version, digest, geometry and quote validation tests PASS
critical negation, modality, amount and date parity tests PASS
privacy, secret exclusion and source-rights tests PASS
